design: One rule, one identity, every entry point. (A) The link's identity: a new module packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-use.ts gives every link one set of keys with the parser discovery already trusts (github:<owner>/<name> lower-case on the install's git hosts, whatever the spelling: https, ssh, scp, .git, www, a /tree/... tail; folder:<real path> lower-case on Windows), plus for a folder its git root and its origin remote's repository key (found by reading files: walk up to .git, read .git/config; no git process runs in the person's folder), plus GitHub's repository id when it was read. Two links are the same when a key matches or one folder is inside the other. A project uses its every repos entry; a project joined into another counts as that one; a removed project (Undo of its creation) uses nothing. (B) On this computer, every way of linking asks this index before anything is written: New project (POST /projects and the chat's port, createProjectRecord), project.create from chat, voice and the palette (plan and run, through a new repositoryUse port), Sources' accept and scan, and the Data tab's GitHub import. When an active project uses the link, nothing is created and the person reads one sentence: 'o/site is already the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.' The New project dialog shows it with Open Site, Add to Site (when a brief or goal was typed) and Cancel. Open switches to Site. Add to sends the brief to Site's planner (POST /projects/:id/intake), which now gets Site's tasks as quoted data and is told to plan only what is new, as its own part (milestone); the plan card arrives in the Inbox as for any brief. Chat gets the same sentence as the tool's answer and can switch (project.switch) and add tasks there. Sources show 'Already the project "Site"' with Open instead of a raw 'duplicate' and ids. The import answers the sentence. (C) From the repository itself: if no project here uses it, the create reads the repository with the person's token (one contents read of .forerunner/project.json on the default branch, one list of open pull requests and their hidden marks, both of which exist today). A project id there that is not on this computer (nor joined into or taken over by one here) means another computer's Forerunner project: 'o/kite is already used by the Forerunner project "Kite club" on another computer. Take it over only if that project is no longer used.' with Take it over and Cancel; the name comes from the marker, is cut at 60 characters, scanned and quoted (else 'another Forerunner project'). Take it over creates the project with settings.took_over {project, name, at}; its next docs pull request (the intake's set or the scaffold) replaces exactly that marker with its own and says so in one line of the PR body; nothing of the other project's on GitHub is pushed to, commented on, closed or listed (W15-01 holds). If GitHub cannot be read, the creation goes on and the project's Overview says it later, once this computer's copy shows another project's marker ('o/kite is also used by the Forerunner project "Kite club" on another computer.' with Take it over, command repo.take_over). This handles forerunner-sandbox: its main names a deleted bench's 'Kite club'. Run C promises no sharing in words, because nothing in the app can share yet; wave 8 adds 'Ask to join' (on a shared store a card to the project's owner; across stores, ask its owner for an invitation) and the status issue as the live source with its writers' logins and last activity, and its AGENTS.md tells other people and agents not to start a second project. (D) Projects that already share a repository or folder on this computer (made before the rule) are shown, not stopped: each Overview says '"Site" and "Kite club" both work in o/site.' with Make one project; until then both work as today and W15-01 keeps their pull requests apart. Make one project opens a dialog that lists each project (open and done tasks, open pull requests, spent so far in CHF, budget per session, project budget, who merges, what research reads), chooses none for the person, names each setting that differs, and is disabled with a sentence while a session runs, a plan card of a closing project is open or a merge is in flight. Its command project.join moves, in one transaction, the closing project's tasks (with their milestones after the kept project's, dependencies, branches and pull request links), the cards about them and its open cards, queued notes, merge records, lessons, decisions and accepted source proposals into the kept project, shares its data, and archives the closing project as 'Joined into "Site" on 9 Nov.' with its link kept for Undo; its sessions, changes, chat and spending stay where they are, readable from its page, which the kept project's Overview links ('Includes the work of "Kite club".'). The kept project reads the closing project's id as its own in pull request marks and docs branches (settings.joined_from), so the moved open pull requests merge from its Overview and its status goes to one status pull request again; nothing on GitHub is edited. No ledger row moves and no cap changes: the kept project's Costs shows what the closed one spent as its own line. Undo in Changes moves everything back and reopens it (after a restart too). (E) A bigger project with parts is one project whose milestones are the parts: the data model needs nothing new; the only addition is that a new part comes in through Add to (a plan that knows what the project already has). (F) W15-01's legacy rule is kept as the fail-closed guard for pairs made before the rule and simplified: soleLinkedProject and its own comparator and 5000-row scan go; the docs paths ask the one index ('the one project here that uses this repository', joined ones counting as it, removed ones as others) and an unmarked docs pull request also needs this computer's copy's marker to name no other project (stricter). Make one project ends a legacy pair; wave 8's status issue later removes the status half altogether. Run C builds A to F in two areas: onerepo-link (identity, every entry point, the repository read and take-over, Add to, the legacy rule) and onerepo-join (Make one project, after onerepo-link). Wave 8 takes over: Ask to join, the status issue as the cross-computer signal and its key, AGENTS.md's line, one issue per repository, and the removal of the status pull request with its held path.
alternatives_rejected: A status branch and status pull request per project on one repository (fr/status-<project>): two pull requests change one docs/status.md and conflict on merge (the W15-112 question); with one project per repository it is not needed.
Ask 'Create a second project anyway?' when a repository is in use: the owner said there should not be two projects on one repository; a button for it would make the exception the habit.

Refuse every repository whose marker names a project that is not on this computer (no take-over): it blocks the owner's own fresh install on forerunner-sandbox, whose marker names a deleted bench home's 'Kite club', and anyone whose earlier install is gone.

Decide by ourselves from recent activity whether the other computer's project is abandoned: that is guessing; the person decides with the facts (name, open pull requests; wave 8 adds the last activity from the status issue).

Write a new file into every repository now (an owner file with the login): wave 8's status issue and AGENTS.md already say who manages it, and .forerunner/project.json already names the project; a second file means one more docs pull request in every repository.
Promise 'ask its owner to share it with you' in run C: nothing in the app can share a project until wave 8 (design section 5 rule 9: no promise the code does not keep).

Make one project by re-pointing every row, sessions and cost ledger included: it rewrites the ledger that caps are measured on and the change history, and the kept project's cap would jump at once; history stays readable on the closed project instead.

Make one project by reading both ids in every per-project query (an alias everywhere): it touches every read (tasks, sessions, costs, chat, cards) for a rare case; aliases are read only where GitHub marks and docs branches carry the old id.

Hold legacy duplicates (no new sessions) until they are made one: it stops work the owner did not ask to stop; W15-01 already keeps their pull requests apart (owner question 2 keeps the alternative open).
Separate projects for parts of a monorepo (one per subfolder): the owner said parts of a bigger project are one project; milestones hold the parts.

Normalise every stored repos entry with a migration: it changes rows nobody touched; the identity compares spellings instead and new links are stored in the canonical form only where today's code already does.

Store GitHub's repository id on the project row whenever repoFor reads the repository: a write in the executor's path bumps the row's version and conflicts with a person's settings edit; the id is read at the check and kept in memory for the daemon's life.

Run git (rev-parse, remote get-url) in a linked folder to find its root and origin: a hostile repository's git config can run commands (core.fsmonitor and the like); reading .git and .git/config as files gives the same facts without running anything.

decisions: One identity for a link (new packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-use.ts): identityOf(entry) -> keys from parseRepoLocator/repoKey (host-checked, lower-case, every spelling) and folderKey (real path, lower-case on Windows), a folder's git root and its origin's repository key (read from .git and .git/config as files), and GitHub's repository id when read; projectsUsing(store, identity) over active projects, a joined project counting as the one it joined (settings.joined_from of the kept project, written by onerepo-join; read here) and a removed project (archived by Undo of its creation) using nothing; projectIdsOf(project) = [id, ...joined_from]. Why: discovery's keys already cover every spelling (ADR 0056 point 3); one function means New project, chat, Sources, import and W15-01 agree.

The check runs before anything is written, at the one creation path (createProjectRecord: POST /projects, Sources' accept, the chat's port) and in project.create's plan and run (a new repositoryUse port in packages/commands/src/types.ts, so chat is refused before a read-back), and in importGitHubRepo. Refusal: ForerunnerError 'validation', HTTP 409, details {cause: 'repository_in_use', projectId, projectName} (the UI's buttons use the id; the person never sees it). Why: one gate, no row, no change-log row, no docs pull request for a refused link.

The words (design section 5): 'o/site is already the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.'; for a folder 'This folder is already used by the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.' Buttons: Open Site, Add to Site (only with a brief or goal), Cancel. Chat gets the same sentence as the tool's answer; project.create's definition says to offer that project (project.switch). Why: the owner's 'in an intelligent way': the person is led to the project that exists, from every entry point.

Add to: POST /projects/:id/intake {brief} (exists). The intake's message for a project with tasks gains a quoted block 'Already in the project (data, between the markers):' with each task as '- "<title>" (<status in words>)', at most 40 then 'and N more', and its instructions one line 'Plan only work that is not already in the project; a new part is its own milestone.' An open plan card answers 'A plan for "Site" waits for your answer. Answer it first.' (no id). Why: a bigger project with parts is one project whose milestones are the parts; milestones exist, so this is all that is needed now.

From the repository itself, read what exists today and what wave 8 keeps: .forerunner/project.json on the default branch (getFile) and the hidden marks of open pull requests (listPullRequests: project= in the mark; fr/intake-<id>-docs branch names). A project id there that is not a row on this install (any status), nor joined into or taken over by a project here, is another computer's project. Run C writes nothing new into repositories. Why: the marker is wave 8's status issue key K; the marks exist since W15-01/W15-08; a new file would cost every repository a docs pull request.

Another computer's project: 'o/kite is already used by the Forerunner project "Kite club" on another computer. Take it over only if that project is no longer used.' (no name known: 'by another Forerunner project'), buttons Take it over / Cancel; Take it over's line: 'This project becomes the repository's; "Kite club"'s pull requests stay as they are.' POST /projects with takeOver {project: <the id the refusal named>} creates it with settings.took_over {project, name, at}; a takeOver naming another id than the repository names now is refused again. Why: forerunner-sandbox's marker names a deleted bench project, so refusing outright would block the owner's fresh install; the person decides, nothing is guessed. No 'ask to share' words before wave 8 builds sharing (design section 5 rule 9).

Take-over effects: the project's next docs pull request (the intake's set on its own branch, or the scaffold) replaces a marker that names exactly the taken-over id (writeInstallMarker gains replace: <id>; any other project's marker is still never overwritten) and its body says 'This repository was the Forerunner project "Kite club"; it is now "<name>"'s.' Nothing of the other project is pushed to, commented on, closed or listed (W15-01); while its status pull request is open this project's status stays in the app with D1-9's words. Why: the repository then tells every computer which project it is.

An existing project whose copy's marker (this computer's copy of the default branch, read as a file) names another computer's project gets one Overview line 'o/kite is also used by the Forerunner project "Kite club" on another computer.' with Take it over (new command repo.take_over, reversible); no card. Covers projects made before the rule and creations made while GitHub could not be read. Why: visible, not blocking; the person decides.

GitHub unreachable, no token or the repository unreadable at creation: the local check still runs; the repository check is skipped without a word at creation (it cannot know) and the Overview line above appears once the copy shows another marker. Why: never block creating on GitHub's answer; never claim what was not read.

W15-01's legacy rule, simplified: soleLinkedProject and its comparator and per-call scan go; the docs paths and the daemon's docs rows ask the index: an unmarked status or scaffold pull request is this project's only when it is the one project on this install using the repository (joined ones count as it, removed ones as others: fail closed as before) and this computer's copy's marker names no other project (new, stricter). isProjectDocsPr/isProjectStatusPr read projectIdsOf (a joined project's mark and intake branch are the kept project's). Why: the task asks to simplify where the rule makes it moot without weakening it; a legacy pair now has an end (onerepo-join).

The Docs row of a status kept in the app because another project's status pull request is open: 'Kept in the app while "A"'s status pull request is open on GitHub.' (another computer's: 'while another project's status pull request is open on GitHub; close it there to have this one's there.'). Why: D1-9; the words of the setting-off case stay.

A URL on a git host this install does not use is refused at link: 'Forerunner works with repositories on github.com, not gitlab.com. Link a GitHub repository or a folder.' Why: today it is silently linked as GitHub's repository of the same owner and name.

Renamed or transferred repositories: RepoInfo gains id (GitHub's numeric id; github.ts toRepo, MemoryGitHost, the fake host); the check reads the id of the new link and of the projects here linked to repositories on the same host (at most 20 reads, kept in memory for the daemon's life; unreadable -> keys only); the marker, when merged, already names the project whatever the repository's name. Why: GitHub redirects an old name, so two names can be one repository.

Security: the marker and pull request bodies are repository content: parsed strictly (marker schema 1, a URI-encoded mark), a name cut at 60 characters with control characters removed, passed through the injection scan (flagged -> 'another Forerunner project'), shown in quotes, and in chat only inside the tool's answer as quoted data, never in a model's instructions; folder identity reads files only, no git process in the person's folder; GitHub reads use the configured host and token, never the page reader. Why: the rules for every design.

U-037 (projects linked to a folder): a folder inside another project's folder, or a clone of its repository, is that project.
U-006 (Data tab import): an import of a repository another project uses answers the sentence.

problems: [major] D1-11: Two projects that already share a repository on this computer (live check 2 and the benches made them; nothing stopped it before onerepo-link) cannot become one: nothing tells the person, tasks cannot move between projects (no such command) and W15-01 keeps the second project's status in the app for as long as the first one's status pull request is open. Owner's words: "There should not be 2 projects in one repo." Where: packages/commands/src/commands/ (task.*, project.switch, project.create, repo.create only); packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts (no such line); packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:910-919.

[major] D1-12: Doing it by hand loses work: a task's pull request, merge record, cards and branch are bound to its project (packages/state/src/schema.ts:212, :344, :822; packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:2893 marks project=<id> in the pull request body; docs.ts:179-180 the intake branch fr/intake-<id>-docs), so cancelling one project's tasks and adding them again to the other drops their open pull requests, reviews and spend history. Owner's words: "If there are multiple people and agents, and even if they are working on different parts of a bigger project, they should be working on one project." Where: as listed.

[minor] D1-13: A project that is closed into another has no words of its own: the project status sentence knows no such state (packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts) and an archived project reads only as '<name> (removed)' (packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts:270-290, server.ts:2505). Owner's words: "Make it such that multiple projects are not done on one repo, in an intelligent way." Where: as listed.
decisions: Shown, not stopped: each project of a set that shares a repository or folder (onerepo-link's index) gets one Overview line '"Site" and "Kite club" both work in o/site.' with Make one project; meanwhile both keep working as today and W15-01 keeps their pull requests apart. Why: keep today's behaviour where the owner did not decide (owner question 1 keeps the alternative).
The person picks the project to keep; no default is selected and the button stays disabled until one is. Why: 'without guessing'.

Command project.join {keep, close: [ids]} (new file packages/commands/src/commands/project-join.ts; risk medium, reversible; the dialog's press is the yes, chat reads it back with Yes and No). Only projects that share a repository or folder can be joined. Why: D1 only, no general merge of unrelated projects.

What moves, in one store transaction (SQLite and Postgres): the closing project's tasks of every status (ids, dependencies, branches, pr_url kept), its milestones after the kept project's (order_index offset), the cards about those tasks and its open cards, its queued notes, merge records, lessons, decisions and accepted source proposals; its data assets add the kept project to project_ids. What stays on the closing project, readable: sessions, cost-ledger rows, changes, chat and answered project cards. The closing project is archived with settings.joined_into {project, at}, its repos cleared and kept as settings.was_linked for Undo; the kept project's settings.joined_from gains its id. Why: the ledger is the truth caps are measured on and is never rewritten; history is not lost; task ids are what worktrees, branches and marks name, so nothing on disk or on GitHub has to change.

Open pull requests keep working: the moved tasks keep their pull requests and merge records; the kept project reads the closing project's id as its own in pull request marks and docs branches through onerepo-link's projectIdsOf, so the closing project's status, scaffold and intake docs pull requests are the kept one's (one status pull request again) and its task pull requests merge from the kept project's Overview. Nothing on GitHub is edited. Why: no write to GitHub for a local reorganisation.

Refused in words, with the button disabled, while: a session runs on either project ('A session is working on "Kite club". Make one project when it ends.'); a plan card of a closing project is open ('The plan of "Kite club" waits for your answer. Answer it first.'); a merge of one of its pull requests is in flight ('A pull request of "Kite club" is being merged. Try again in a minute.'); the projects share no repository or folder. Why: no row moves under a running worker.

Settings: the kept project's settings apply to the moved work; the dialog names each that differs in one line (budget per session, project budget, who merges, what research reads), e.g. 'Who merges: "Site"'s setting applies to the moved work: you press Merge.' Why: no silent change of a limit or a rule; the person sees it before pressing.

Money: no cap, budget or ledger row changes; the kept project's cap keeps measuring its own ledger; the closing project's spend stays booked to it and shows on the kept project's Costs as 'Spent in "Kite club" before it joined: CHF 3.20'. Why: no budget is passed and spend stays visible in CHF.

The closed project's page: status sentence 'Joined into "Site" on 9 Nov.' with Open Site, no Start or New task; its sessions, changes, costs and chat remain readable; the kept project's Overview says 'Includes the work of "Kite club".' linking to it; Home lists only the kept project. Why: history stays one click away.

Undo (Changes): moves every moved row back (and rows made on the kept project since for a moved task), reopens the closing project with its link and removes it from joined_from; refused in words while a session runs on the kept project or a moved task's merge is in flight; works after a restart. Why: a safe way is a reversible one.
